## Activities

- {{< iconify fa6-solid people-line size=18px >}} **Monday and Wednesday**:
Modern cryptography and review
  - Understand why the one-time pad cannot scale to long messages
  - Learn how a pseudorandom generator expands a short key
  - Explore how a stream cipher depends on a unique nonce
  - Review the security concepts and code from all prior weeks
  - Continued highlighting of the concept of a "security synapse"
  - Student presentations that feature:
    - Explanation of a high-level concept behind computational security
    - In-class activity that connects concepts to real-world scenarios
    - Hands-on examples of the operation of a pseudorandom generator
- **Tuesday**: No classes due to All-College Programming Day
- {{< iconify fa6-solid people-line size=18px >}} **Friday**: Complete In-Person
Assessment Two during the class session
- {{< iconify fa6-solid diagram-project size=18px >}} **Friday**: Complete
Midterm Executable Examination Two in the laboratory session
  - **Date**: Friday, November 6, 2026
  - **Time**: 2:30 -- 4:30 PM
  - **Location**: Alden 109
  - Use GitHub, VS Code, and your laptop to complete the examination
  - Cite external sources, including artificial intelligence coding
  assistants, that you use during the examination
